text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure is considered high (hypertension) when it is consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg, according to guidelines from the American Heart Association and the CDC.
snippet_highlighted_words: consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg

list.snippet: Normal: Less than 120 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic
Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic
Stage 1 Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): 130–139 mm Hg systolic or 80–89 mm Hg diastolic
Stage 2 Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): 140 mm Hg or higher systolic or 90 mm Hg or higher diastolic

Severe Hypertension / Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 mm Hg systolic and/or higher than 120 mm Hg diastolic (Seek emergency care if accompanied by symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, or numbness)
Systolic (Top number): Measures the pressure in your arteries when your heart beats.
Diastolic (Bottom number): Measures the pressure in your arteries when your heart rests between beats.
